subject: Architecture
title: Mesopotamian Ziggurats: Stairways to Heaven
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mesopotamian Ziggurats: Stairways to Heaven usable.

hook.text: The Sumerians built massive stepped towers to bring their temples closer to the gods.

buildup.text: Ziggurats rose in tiers of sun-dried brick, each level smaller than the one below.

discovery.text: The Great Ziggurat of Ur stood 100 feet tall and was rebuilt by Saddam Hussein in the 1980s.

twist.text: Only priests could climb to the top shrine. The public worshipped from ground level.

climax.text: The Biblical Tower of Babel was almost certainly inspired by a real Babylonian ziggurat.

punchline.text: They built upward because they believed the gods were listening.

quiz.question: What likely inspired the Biblical Tower of Babel?
